decision: the 3-booted cap counts only ClaudioBot-UX-1..3; the already-booted iPhone 17 Pro (81E949D3) is the user's and is left alone
why: program forbids touching other devices; shutting it down could disrupt the user

decision: findings live in docs/ux-program/findings.tsv; ledger.tsv tracks steps
why: one file per concern keeps "next unfinished step" a one-line read

decision: scenario registry is TypeScript data (bin/scenarios.ts) and sessions.md is generated from it
why: one source for the setup, the rubric text and its mechanical check; a hand-written doc would drift from the checks

decision: a failed rubric item is a finding (exit 0); only a failed precondition fails the scenario (exit 2)
why: the audit wants findings recorded, and must never judge a situation it could not produce

decision: scenarios answer every permission card Allow once and record the tap
why: subagent and long Bash calls ask in default mode; a user would approve them, and auto mode would add a classifier as a second variable

decision: the phone leaves a thread (unwatch) before unread is judged and reopens it (watch after) to judge the thread
why: the bridge never marks a watched thread unread (catalog.ts), so a watcher that never leaves cannot see unread at all

decision: a lease's staleness is judged by its heartbeat only, not by pid liveness
why: lease acquire from the CLI exits right away, so another agent's lease has no live pid; the heartbeat is the one signal every holder keeps

decision: pairing stops at the app's confirmation; the Pair tap is left to an agent with the simulator tool, and no Debug auto-pair hook was added to the app
why: Step 0 changes no product code; an auto-confirm launch argument is a product call for the iOS owner

decision: S1 pins run_in_background false on its Agent calls and S1b pins true, each checked as a precondition
why: Claude Code's Agent tool defaults to async subagents and haiku chose either mode across runs; unpinned, S1 judged a different situation each time

decision: long foreground calls in scenarios use perl -e 'sleep N', not sleep N
why: Claude Code blocks a leading foreground sleep ("Blocked: standalone sleep 30"), so a sleep-based call never holds the turn

decision: in S8 the background command finishing is the judged outcome, not a precondition
why: the subagent started it (the situation was produced) and it never finished; reporting that as a failed precondition would hide the finding

decision: add a Debug-only launch argument that confirms a pairing link without the tap, for the simulator lane
why: simctl has no input; the simulator lane (S3, Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, dark mode, iPad checks) needs a paired app with no human; Debug-only keeps Release behavior unchanged

decision: reference study observes Claude Code desktop through its docs, on-disk session state and the CLI it wraps, not screen capture
why: computer-use needs a live user approval prompt, which would block an autonomous run

decision: simulator screenshots may show real session titles; they stay in the temp evidence folder, are never committed, and findings never quote real titles
why: the Sessions area must be audited on the real list (S7 mixes real and run sessions); keeping titles out of the repo and reports protects privacy without hiding the screen under audit

decision: X-ipad is judged by reading the app's size-class and split-view code plus iPhone landscape screenshots, and reported as a coverage gap
why: the program allows only the 3 iPhone pool devices; an iPad pool device would need the operator to allow cloning one

decision: ux-audit run caps at 6 rounds; when a run ends before two dry rounds, its survivors go into findings.tsv and the next run dedupes against them, continuing the loop
why: one run already took 3.3 h and 601 agents; findings per round fell 41,32,29,21,16,13 so the tail is real but shrinking

decision: Step 3 for Sessions starts on the 81 P0/P1 survivors while the next audit run continues in parallel; P2s are folded into a fix group only when it already touches their files, else they wait for the backlog
why: fixes land on main through worktrees and do not change the code the audit reads in this worktree; waiting hours for a dry run would idle the program

decision: an extra iPhone 17 Pro (D91C2F8B) was found booted during the audit; no auditor commanded it (transcripts checked), other Claude sessions on this Mac use it, so it is left alone
why: never touch devices outside the pool
